evidence: delete-product.service.ts: DeleteProductService.execute(productId) builds `new DeleteProductCommand(productId)` and calls `this.commandBus.execute(command)`, so it uses the module's command abstraction.
delete-product.command-handler.ts: DeleteProductCommandHandler.execute is the only place that checks `productRepository.exists(productId)` and throws NotFoundException before calling `delete`.

delete-product.dto.ts: DeleteProductDto { id: string } belongs to the same use case, but DeleteProductService.execute takes a raw string instead. This is a minor naming and usage inconsistency, not a split of concerns.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All four files handle a single concern, deleting a product. The service turns a call into a DeleteProductCommand and sends it through the CommandBus. The handler checks that the product exists, then deletes it. The command and DTO are plain data carriers for the same use case. The only invariant, that the product must exist before deletion, is enforced in one place: DeleteProductCommandHandler.execute. No file in the unit skips the module's own abstractions, because the service goes through the command/handler pipeline instead of calling the repository directly. One small inconsistency: DeleteProductDto declares `id`, but DeleteProductService.execute takes a raw `productId: string` and never uses the DTO. Whether that matters depends on how the controller uses it. It doesn't split the concerns or duplicate a rule, so it isn't a failure. The handler's dependency on infrastructure (ProductRepository) is an import-direction question, which is out of scope for this rule.
